chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muawiya ibn Hakim from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal said:
I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'A man gives me an advance for food, but when the time comes, I do not have food. Can I give him dirhams equal to its value?' He said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Can a seller pay cash instead of delivering the specific goods if they fail to provide them on time after receiving an advance?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility in settling debts of advance-paid foodstuff, permitting the debtor to pay the monetary value (dirhams) if the specific goods are unavailable at the due date. It highlights the practical application of *istisna'* and *salam* contracts in early Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the obligation can be discharged in currency when the original commodity is not at hand, reflecting the Imams' pragmatic approach to commercial transactions.
